lines.japanese: 「ぷあっ！」
lines.english: “Pwah!”

lines.japanese: 気が付いたとき、僕は狭い浴槽の中で息苦しさに湯を撥ねちらかしていた。
lines.english: When awareness returned, I was thrashing in the cramped bathtub, splashing water everywhere as I fought for breath.

lines.japanese: 「がは……こふっ、こふっ……」
lines.english: “Gah… kh—kh…”

lines.japanese: 咳きこむごとに津波を起こす蛍光グリーンの海。
lines.english: A fluorescent-green sea, raising a tsunami with every cough.

lines.japanese: 口だか鼻だか分からない気管のどこか奥の方で、ハーブの香りが断続的に爆発する。
lines.english: Somewhere deep in the airways behind either my mouth or my nose, I could not tell which, the scent of herbs exploded at intervals.

lines.japanese: 「っはあ、はあ、はあ……」
lines.english: “Hah… hah… hah…”

lines.japanese: 咳が落ちついてくると、僕は浴槽のふちに手をかけて、その上にぐったりと顎を載せた。
lines.english: As the coughing subsided, I caught the rim of the tub and slumped there with my chin resting on it.

lines.japanese: 荒い呼吸が波のまにまに同調して、赤く火照った肩を揺らす。
lines.english: My ragged breathing fell into rhythm with the waves, rocking my flushed red shoulders.

lines.japanese: びっくりした。入浴中に≪召喚≫なんて、向こうのひとたちも少しはこちらの都合を考えてほしい。
lines.english: That had startled me. A Summoning in the middle of my bath—the people over there could at least spare a thought for what I might be doing.

lines.japanese: 湯気と一緒に、裸の体から金色の粒子が立ちのぼってゆく。
lines.english: Golden particles rose from my naked body with the steam.

lines.japanese: 僕は浴槽のへりにしがみつきながら、洗い場のタイルに目を落とす。
lines.english: Still clinging to the bathtub, I lowered my eyes to the tiled floor outside it.

lines.japanese: 耳の奥には、まだ戦士たちの怒号や鬨の声がこびりついている……気がした。
lines.english: The roars and battle cries of the warriors still clung to the back of my ears… or seemed to.

lines.japanese: 大地のふるえ。戦場のとどろき。
lines.english: The trembling earth. The thunder of the battlefield.

lines.japanese: 足の裏には、まだ漠然としたおぞましい違和感が残っている。土色の肌をした亜人種が、その下で醜悪な断末魔をあげて──ぐにゅり。
lines.english: A vague, horrible sensation remained beneath my soles. The earth-skinned demihuman below them had raised a hideous death cry—squelch.

lines.japanese: しかし戦場での陰惨な地獄絵図は、揺れる水面が静まるより早く溶けて霧散する。
lines.english: But that ghastly vision of the battlefield’s hell dissolved and scattered before the rippling water could grow still.

lines.japanese: その記憶は消える間際に、僕がむかし遠足で不注意から踏んづけてしまった小さな甲虫へとリンクした。
lines.english: In the instant before it vanished, the memory linked itself to a small beetle I had carelessly stepped on during a childhood field trip.

lines.japanese: ぺきょっ──足の裏の感触。
lines.english: Crick—the feeling beneath my foot.

lines.japanese: あのとき、あのハナムグリはどうしてあんなところを這いつくばっていたんだろう。羽に怪我でもしてたんだろうか。
lines.english: Why had that flower chafer been crawling around down there? Had one of its wings been hurt?

lines.japanese: 僕はゆらりと背中を伸ばし、平穏を取りもどした浴槽の中で両膝を立てた。
lines.english: I slowly straightened my back and drew up both knees in the bathtub, now peaceful once more.

lines.japanese: 親指で土踏まずのあたりを闇雲に押してみる。
lines.english: With one thumb, I pressed blindly at the arch of my foot.

lines.japanese: どこかのサイトで読んだことがあった。足の裏にはさまざまなツボが集まっていて、第二の心臓なんて呼ばれているらしい。
lines.english: I had read somewhere online that all sorts of pressure points gathered in the soles, which were apparently called the body’s second heart.

lines.japanese: でたらめなマッサージをしながら、僕はなんとなく考えてみた。
lines.english: As I administered my haphazard massage, a thought occurred to me.

lines.japanese: ハナムグリにもいろんな種があるはずだから、もしかしたら、中には花から花へ飛びまわるのが苦手な個体だっているのかもしれない。今度ネットで調べてみよう。
lines.english: There must be many species of flower chafer. Perhaps some individuals were poor at flitting from flower to flower. I would look it up online sometime.

lines.japanese: しばらくして湯船から身を揚げたとき、軽いめまいが僕を襲った。
lines.english: A little later, when I raised myself from the bath, a mild dizziness overtook me.

lines.japanese: どうやらのぼせてしまうぐらいの時間、僕の体は湯に浸かっていたらしい。浴槽に置いた手で、立ちあがった自分の体重を支えた。
lines.english: Apparently my body had remained in the water long enough to overheat. One hand braced on the tub, I supported my weight as I stood.

lines.japanese: 「もう……寝ようかな……」
lines.english: “Maybe… I should go to bed…”

lines.japanese: 期末考査も四日目。連日の睡眠不足が、折からの湯あたりで重たげな倦怠感となってのしかかってきた。
lines.english: It was the fourth day of final exams. Successive nights of too little sleep, joined now by the heat of the bath, bore down upon me as a heavy lassitude.

lines.japanese: 三年生のこの時期、志望校の入試対策一本に勝負を絞って、校内のテストは軽く流すような生徒も少なくない。先生たちだってそんな風潮を黙認している。
lines.english: At this point in their final year, plenty of students staked everything on preparing for their chosen university’s entrance exam and merely coasted through the school tests. Even the teachers tacitly accepted the custom.

lines.japanese: だけど、受験日まで残っているか分からない僕にとっては、これがこっちの世界での最後の戦になるかもしれない。
lines.english: But I did not know whether I would last until entrance-exam day. This might be my final battle in this world.

lines.japanese: 「いや……やっぱり頑張ろ……」
lines.english: “No… I should try after all…”

lines.japanese: 平均７０点以上取るという“残務処理”のひとつを思いだして、僕はドアを開けた。
lines.english: Remembering one item of my Unfinished Business—score an average of at least seventy—I opened the door.

lines.japanese: 実際テストは面倒だけど、でも嫌いというほどじゃない。
lines.english: Tests were a nuisance, certainly, but I did not dislike them.

lines.japanese: たとえるなら、ぶらりと立ちよったゲームセンターの対戦ものに似てるのかもしれない。
lines.english: If I had to compare them to something, perhaps they resembled a competitive game in an arcade I had wandered into by chance.

lines.japanese: いい点を取ったからって何か得するわけじゃない。でも誰かに勝つっていうことはなんとなく……嬉しいものだ。
lines.english: A good score gained me nothing. Yet there was something… pleasant about defeating someone.

lines.japanese: 頑張った分だけ数字に表れる。こんなにも公平なことって、世の中には意外と少ないと思うんだ。
lines.english: Every ounce of effort appeared in the number. I think the world contains surprisingly few things so fair.

lines.japanese: 浴室を出た僕は、軽く水気を吹きとった体に下着とＴシャツだけまとって、あとは籠からバスタオルとスウェットの上下を掴んで、さっさと蒸した脱衣所から逃げだした。
lines.english: I left the bathroom, quickly dried my body, and put on only underwear and a T-shirt. Snatching my bath towel and sweats from the basket, I fled the sweltering dressing room.

lines.japanese: 明かりの灯らない１２月の廊下は、夏休みの図書館よりも冷えこんでいた。その突きはなされたような温度が、風呂上がりには心地良い。
lines.english: Unlit in December, the hallway was colder than a library during summer vacation. After the bath, its aloof chill felt pleasant.

lines.japanese: ひとの気配がない夜の静寂。
lines.english: The silence of a night with no human presence.

lines.japanese: 家主である叔父さん夫婦は出張中。五つ下の妹は、たぶん二階の自室で、薄幸のヒロインが最後には報われる古い少女漫画でも読んでいるんだろう。
lines.english: My aunt and uncle, the owners of the house, were away on business. My sister, five years younger than I, was probably upstairs in her room reading some old girls’ manga where the long-suffering heroine found happiness at last.

lines.japanese: 僕は無人の廊下にスウェットを落とし、濡れた頭をタオルで掻きまぜた。
lines.english: I dropped my sweats in the empty hallway and tousled my wet hair with the towel.

lines.japanese: 途中、湯あたりの波がひとつ首筋を這いのぼってきたので、手を止めて寄りそうように壁へもたれた。
lines.english: A wave of heat-sickness crawled up my neck. I stopped my hand and leaned against the wall as though drawing close to it for comfort.

lines.japanese: 僕は満員の地下鉄の中でも、扉に身を預けるのが好きだった。
lines.english: Even on a packed subway train, I had always liked surrendering my weight to the doors.

lines.japanese: 昼よりも夜が好き。夏よりも冬が好き。大勢よりも独りが好き。たぶんね。
lines.english: I preferred night to day. Winter to summer. Solitude to a crowd. Probably.

lines.japanese: やがて、めまいは去った。
lines.english: At last, the dizziness passed.

lines.japanese: しかし熱を帯びた気だるさがどうにも拭いきれず、しばらく凍える闇の中で立ちつくしていた。
lines.english: But the fevered languor would not leave me, and for a while I stood motionless in the freezing dark.

lines.japanese: 湯気に曇ったような思考の中、ふやけた裸足の底にわだかまる悪寒があった。
lines.english: In thoughts clouded as though by steam, I felt a chill lodged beneath my water-softened bare foot.

lines.japanese: いったん足を持ちあげ、もう片方の足に重心を移しかえる。
lines.english: I raised that foot and shifted my weight onto the other.

lines.japanese: 僕は飛べないハナムグリと、あの遠足の日を思いだしていた。
lines.english: I was remembering the flower chafer that could not fly, and the day of that field trip.

lines.japanese: 名前は忘れたけど、どこかの山間にある大きな自然公園だった。
lines.english: I have forgotten its name, but it was a large nature park somewhere in the mountains.

lines.japanese: 季節は……６年生に上がってすぐだから、そう、桜が散って遊歩道がまだらに汚れていたころだ。
lines.english: The season was… just after we entered sixth grade. Yes: the cherry blossoms had fallen, leaving the paths mottled and untidy.

lines.japanese: フランス国旗みたいにカラフルなレジャーシートの上で、めいめいの弁当を広げる体操着姿の子供たち。
lines.english: Children in gym clothes spread their lunches over picnic sheets as colorful as the French flag.

lines.japanese: 体操着のゼッケンには、名字の上に学年とクラスを入れる決まりになっていた。
lines.english: By rule, the name patch on each uniform bore a student’s grade and class above the family name.

lines.japanese: 一学期の始業式の前日、叔母はアイロン台の上に僕がそれまで使っていた『５年２組』の体操着を広げ、ゆっくりサインペンを滑らせた。
lines.english: The day before the opening ceremony, my aunt spread the gym shirt I had worn until then—marked ‘Class 5-2’—across the ironing board and slowly drew her felt-tip pen over it.

lines.japanese: 数字の５の左穴が塞がれて、それはたちまち最上級生のユニフォームに生まれかわった。
lines.english: She filled in the open left side of the five. In an instant, it was reborn as the uniform of a sixth grader, now in the highest grade.

lines.japanese: ──ほら、すごい。魔法みたいでしょ。
lines.english: —There. Amazing, isn’t it? Just like magic.

lines.japanese: 叔母や叔父は僕のことを、血を分けた小鳩と分けへだてなく可愛がってくれたけど、その分ちょっと過保護気味というか、幼い年齢のように扱うところがあった。
lines.english: My aunt and uncle loved me no differently from their own daughter, Kobato. Perhaps for that very reason, they tended to shelter me and treat me as though I were younger than I was.

lines.japanese: ──うわあ、おばさんすごいね。
lines.english: —Wow, Auntie. You’re amazing.

lines.japanese: だから僕は彼女たちの期待に応えて、第二反抗期なんかとは無縁のあどけない子供に育つ必要があった。
lines.english: And so I had to answer their expectations by growing into an innocent child untouched by adolescent rebellion.

lines.japanese: だけどあの遠足の日、クラスで二番目に体の大きかった大谷君が、レジャーシートにあぐらをかきながら僕を見上げて言った。
lines.english: But on the day of the field trip, Ōtani, the second-largest boy in our class, looked up at me from where he sat cross-legged on the picnic sheet.

lines.japanese: ──羽田、おまえ５年なんだろ。こっち入んなよな。
lines.english: —Haneda, you’re a fifth grader, right? Go sit over there.

lines.japanese: 胸に丸々とした６を貼りつけている同じ班のみんなも、まだ靴を脱いでいない僕を見てくすくす笑った。
lines.english: The other children in my group, each with a plump six pasted to their chest, looked at me standing there with my shoes still on and giggled.

lines.japanese: 僕も一緒に笑いたかったけど、頬が引きつれて上手く笑えなかった。
lines.english: I wanted to laugh with them, but my cheeks had drawn tight and would not make the proper shape.

lines.japanese: 担任の中里先生が大谷君を詰めさせて、僕はその隣りに座ったけど、それからバスに乗って帰るまでのあいだ、僕は腹痛を訴えてずっとおなかを押さえていた。
lines.english: Our teacher, Mr. Nakazato, made Ōtani move over, and I sat beside him. But from then until we boarded the bus home, I complained of a stomachache and kept both hands pressed to my belly.

lines.japanese: 家に帰ると僕はすぐに体操着を脱ぎ、それを学習机の上に広げた。
lines.english: The moment I reached home, I stripped off my gym shirt and spread it over my desk.

lines.japanese: 鍵をかけた部屋の中、長らく握っていて皺になったゼッケンを一時間ぐらい見下ろしていたと思う。
lines.english: I locked the door. For what must have been an hour, I stared down at the name patch, wrinkled from being clenched so long in my hand.

lines.japanese: やがて僕は図工用の彫刻刀を握り、ななめに立てた刃をゆっくり引いた。
lines.english: At last I took up a carving knife from my art supplies, angled the blade, and slowly drew it across.

lines.japanese: 刃の通りが悪くてベニア板を削るみたいには思いどおりいかなかったけど、それでも唇を噛みながら幾筋かの傷を作った。
lines.english: It did not pass cleanly through the cloth as it would through plywood, but I bit my lip and managed to cut several gashes.

lines.japanese: 魔法の６の字だけは避けて。
lines.english: I took care to spare only the magical six.

lines.japanese: それからしばらくして精肉工場のパートから帰ってきた叔母に、木版画の授業でうっかり手が滑ってしまったと説明してそれを見せた。
lines.english: Some time later, when my aunt came home from her shift at the meatpacking plant, I showed it to her and explained that my hand had slipped in woodblock-printing class.

lines.japanese: 僕は俯いて叔母と目を合わせなかったから、彼女がどんな顔をしていたかは見えなかった。
lines.english: My head was bowed, my eyes avoiding hers, so I never saw the expression on her face.

lines.japanese: ただ彼女は、甥のぼっちゃん刈りの頭に手を置いて「怪我しなくて良かったね」と言った。
lines.english: She merely rested a hand upon her nephew’s bowl-cut head and said, ‘I’m glad you weren’t hurt.’

lines.japanese: 次の日、朝起きると、僕の枕元には新しいゼッケンのついた体操着が丁寧に畳んで置かれていた。
lines.english: The next morning, I awoke to find my gym shirt neatly folded beside my pillow with a new name patch sewn on.

lines.japanese: 両手で掴んで広げると、ふわっと洗剤のにおいが舞った。
lines.english: When I caught it in both hands and unfolded it, the scent of detergent rose softly.

lines.japanese: 素敵な魔法は解けて、平凡な数字がそこにあった。
lines.english: The lovely spell had broken. An ordinary number waited there.

lines.japanese: 僕は壁から離れて、白い息をひとつ落とした。
lines.english: I pushed away from the wall and let one white breath fall.

lines.japanese: 立ちくらみが引いた代わりに、首の後ろあたりがじんじんする。
lines.english: The faintness was gone, replaced by a prickling at the nape of my neck.

lines.japanese: 明日はテスト最終日だ。こんなところでぼーっと立ちつくしてる場合じゃない。
lines.english: Tomorrow was the final day of exams. I had no business standing here in a daze.

lines.japanese: そして期末考査が終わったあとには、誰もが面倒の種としか思っていない卒業文集作りが待っている。きっと学級委員の僕は、率先して指揮を取らなければならないんだろう。
lines.english: And after finals came the graduation anthology, which everyone regarded as nothing but a source of trouble. As class representative, I would doubtless have to step forward and direct the work.

lines.japanese: 学級委員なんて、なりたくてなったわけじゃないけど、クラスのみんなや担任の先生にこぞって推薦されてしまったから仕方ない。ひとから頼りにされるのは悪い気分じゃないし。
lines.english: I had never wanted to be class representative. But my classmates and our teacher had all nominated me, and there was little I could do. It did not feel unpleasant to have people rely on me.

lines.japanese: でも、せめて副委員長がもうちょっと協力的なら良かったんだけど。
lines.english: Still, it would have helped if the vice class representative were a little more cooperative.
“Haaah…”

lines.japanese: まだ肌の赤みは残っていたけど、僕はのろのろとスウェットを身につけて歩きだした。
lines.english: My skin was still flushed, but I slowly pulled on my sweats and began to walk.

lines.japanese: 暗い廊下を渡りながら思った。そうだ、ちょっと庭先へ下りて体の火照りを静めよう。机へ向かう前に、僕はふと厳しい冬の夜風を浴びておきたくなったんだ。
lines.english: As I crossed the dark hallway, an idea came to me. I would step into the garden and cool my body. Before returning to my desk, I suddenly wanted to feel the severity of the winter night wind.

lines.japanese: ふすまを開けて居間に入る。底冷えした畳の暗室には、どこか人いきれにも似た微妙な空気の滞りがあった。
lines.english: I slid open the partition and entered the living room. The straw mats in the dark, bone-cold room held a faint pocket of stale warmth, almost like the lingering heat of human bodies.

lines.japanese: けれどそんな違和感も、すぐに湯上がりの余熱と芳香にかき消されてしまう。
lines.english: But the lingering heat and fragrance of the bath soon overwhelmed that faint unease.

lines.japanese: だから僕はそんなことなど気にも留めず、明かりさえ付けないまま部屋を横切った。
lines.english: I gave it no further thought and crossed the room without even turning on the light.

lines.japanese: 縁側の障子を開ける。
lines.english: I opened the paper screen onto the veranda.

lines.japanese: 続けてガラス戸。
lines.english: Then the glass door.

lines.japanese: さらにその奥の雨戸。
lines.english: Then the storm shutter beyond it.

lines.japanese: 葉を落としたトチノキがそびえ、そのまわりに植木鉢やプランターの並ぶ小さな植物園が、塀の向こうの街灯によってほの青く照らされていた。
lines.english: A horse chestnut, bare of leaves, towered over a small botanical garden of flowerpots and planters, all faintly lit blue by the streetlamp beyond the wall.

lines.japanese: 風はなかったけれど、有刺鉄線みたいに張りつめた冷たい夜気は、身じろぎしただけで薬用成分にふやけた僕の頬を切りつける。
lines.english: There was no wind, yet the night air was cold and taut as barbed wire. The slightest movement made it cut my cheeks, softened by the medicinal bath.

lines.japanese: 立ちのぼってゆく白い息吹。寒い。けれどいまの僕にはこのぐらいが適温だ。
lines.english: My white breath rose. It was cold. But for me, at that moment, the temperature was exactly right.

lines.japanese: ガラス戸の桟をまたいで、板の間へそっと腰を下ろす。叔父さん自慢の庭は静けさに満ちていた。
lines.english: I stepped over the track of the glass door and gently sat upon the wooden veranda. My uncle’s beloved garden brimmed with silence.

lines.japanese: 頼りなく天に伸びる禿げたトチノキ。薄暗がりの中で鈍く光るアルミのじょうろ。隅でとぐろを巻いたビニールホース。何もかもが静かだ。
lines.english: The naked horse chestnut reached uncertainly toward heaven. An aluminum watering can glimmered dully in the half-light. A vinyl hose lay coiled in one corner. Everything was still.

lines.japanese: 叔母さんが１００円ショップで買ってきた白木のサンダルは、片方だけが遠くにはぐれて引っくりかえっていた。
lines.english: Of the pale wooden sandals my aunt had bought at the hundred-yen store, one lay far from its mate, overturned.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩、しょうがないな……」
lines.english: “Honestly, Kobato…”

lines.japanese: 僕は片足を一方のサンダルに下ろし、そこから手を伸ばして迷子のもう一方を拾った。
lines.english: I lowered one foot into the nearer sandal, then stretched from there to retrieve its wandering mate.

lines.japanese: 小鳩はいつだって叔母さんの家事を進んで手伝うし、兄の贔屓目抜きにして、あの年頃にしてはよく出来た子だと思う。
lines.english: Kobato always volunteered to help my aunt with the housework. Even setting aside a brother’s bias, I thought her remarkably capable for her age.

lines.japanese: でも、たまにこういう子供らしさを痕跡として残すことがある。
lines.english: But now and then, she left behind some trace of childhood like this.

lines.japanese: たぶん、庭に出ていたら電話が鳴ったとか新聞屋の集金が来たとかで、慌てて脱ぎすてたんだろう。そして戻ってきたらそのまま窓をぴしゃり。
lines.english: Perhaps the telephone had rung while she was in the garden, or someone had come to collect the newspaper bill, and she had kicked them off in a hurry. Then she returned and simply slammed the window shut.

lines.japanese: 僕は思わずあたたかな苦笑を浮かべながら、両足にサンダルを履いて夜の庭に立った。
lines.english: A warm, wry smile came over me. I slipped into both sandals and stood in the night garden.

lines.japanese: 塀の向こうから射しこむ常夜灯の明かりに近付いてみると、緑の草葉は艶やかに濡れていた。スプーンみたいな形をしたアロエの葉の底には、小さな水溜まりが佇んでいる。
lines.english: Nearer the glow of the streetlamp beyond the wall, the green leaves shone wet. A small pool rested at the base of an aloe leaf shaped like a spoon.

lines.japanese: しまった。小鳩は水を撒くために庭へ出たんだ。今日は僕の庭当番の日じゃないか。
lines.english: Oh, no. Kobato had come out to water the garden. Today was my turn.

lines.japanese: 叔父さん夫婦が留守のあいだは、僕と妹が交代で庭の管理をしていた（もちろん、ガーデニングを長年の趣味としている叔父さんほど本格的なことはできないけれど）。
lines.english: While my aunt and uncle were away, my sister and I took turns caring for it. Naturally, we could do nothing so serious as my uncle, for whom gardening had been a lifelong hobby.

lines.japanese: 「言ってくれればやるのに……」
lines.english: “You could have told me…”

lines.japanese: だけど、それを僕に言うぐらいなら、さっさと自分で片を付けてしまうのが羽田小鳩という子だった。
lines.english: But Kobato Haneda was the sort of girl who would sooner finish a task herself than trouble herself to tell me about it.

lines.japanese: 彼女の気配りと優しさは分かる。でも、たったひとりの兄である僕にぐらい、言いたいことを言ってほしいと思う。
lines.english: I understood her consideration and kindness. Still, with me at least—her only brother—I wished she would say whatever was on her mind.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は僕に対して、不自然なくらい言葉が足りない。ひとつ屋根の下に暮らしていながら、まったく会話を交わさない日だって少なくないぐらいだ。
lines.english: With me, Kobato was unnaturally sparing of words. Though we lived beneath the same roof, days on which we exchanged not a single word were hardly rare.

lines.japanese: それは、やっぱり、血の繋がった兄妹じゃないから、なのかな……僕はそんなこと気にもしないし、物心ついてからずっと本当の妹だと思って接してきたんだけど。
lines.english: Was it, after all, because we were not brother and sister by blood? I had never cared about that. Ever since I was old enough to know anything, I had treated her as my true sister.

lines.japanese: このところ、しばしば思う。
lines.english: Lately, a thought often came to me.

lines.japanese: 僕がいなくなったあと、彼女は寂しい思いをしてくれるだろうか。
lines.english: After I was gone, would she feel lonely?

lines.japanese: もしさよならを告げたら、彼女は僕を引きとめてくれるだろうか。
lines.english: If I told her goodbye, would she ask me to stay?

lines.japanese: 冬の夜空を見上げる。
lines.english: I looked up at the winter night sky.

lines.japanese: かつて優しいひとたちが、このきらめく宝石の海を指差し、僕の両親はあの中のひとつになったのだと説明した。
lines.english: Long ago, kind people had pointed to that sparkling sea of jewels and explained that my parents had become one of its stars.

lines.japanese: 僕はそれ以上のことを尋ねなかった。それが聞いちゃいけないことだってのは、おさな心になんとなく分かった。
lines.english: I asked nothing more. Even as a small child, I dimly understood that I must not.

lines.japanese: 眉をひそめた大人たちの囁きは、たしかに子供の乏しい語彙では詳らかな意味まで把握できなかった。
lines.english: My meager childhood vocabulary could not, it was true, unravel the exact meaning of the adults’ frowning whispers.

lines.japanese: それでも、外国のひとの言葉がその表情や声色でおぼろげな輪郭ぐらいは推測できるように、たぶん僕はそうやって肌で感じとれたんだと思う。
lines.english: But just as one may infer the rough outline of a foreigner’s words from expression and tone, I think I must have sensed the shape of the truth instinctively.

lines.japanese: 仏壇の写真でしか見たことのない母は、悪い男のひとを好きになって幸せでない人生を終えた。
lines.english: My mother, whom I knew only from the photograph on the family altar, had loved a bad man and reached the end of an unhappy life.

lines.japanese: 仏壇に写真すら据えられていない父は、悪い男と呼ばれたまま家族を不幸にしてどこかへ消えた。
lines.english: My father, whose photograph did not even stand upon the altar, had brought misery to his family, been named a bad man, and vanished somewhere.

lines.japanese: でも大人たちはそのことを必死に隠そうとしているから、僕は何も知らない子供でいるべきだった。
lines.english: But the adults struggled desperately to hide all this. Therefore, I had to remain a child who knew nothing.

lines.japanese: 「すぅーっ……」
lines.english: “Haaaaah…”

lines.japanese: 僕は夜の温度を胸いっぱいに吸いこんだ。よく冷えたミントティーみたいな清涼感が肺に流れこむと、湯疲れした重い頭が冴えてゆく。
lines.english: I breathed in the cold of the night. A freshness like well-chilled mint tea flowed into my lungs and cleared my heavy, bath-weary head.

lines.japanese: すでに凛とした冬が寝巻き代わりのスウェットに染みこんで、温まりすぎた体もほどよく冷えていた。
lines.english: Bracing winter had already seeped into the sweats I wore as pajamas, cooling my overheated body to just the proper degree.

lines.japanese: 「よしっ！」
lines.english: “All right!”

lines.japanese: 僕は両頬に活を入れた。
lines.english: I slapped both cheeks to rouse myself.

lines.japanese: 物思いに耽ってる場合じゃない。明日は期末テスト最終日、世界史と数学が控えている。とくに数学は僕との相性が悪い。今夜は完徹だ。
lines.english: This was no time for brooding. Tomorrow was the last day of finals: world history and mathematics. Mathematics and I were particularly ill matched. I would study through the night.

lines.japanese: 情けないことに、きのうも、おとといも、教科書を睨んでいたらいつの間にか朝日が昇っていたという始末。今夜こそは睡魔に負けずやり遂げよう。
lines.english: Pathetically, both yesterday and the day before, I had started out glaring at my textbooks only to find the sun up before I knew it. Tonight I would resist sleep and see the work through.

lines.japanese: はるか頭上のオリオンに誓ってから、僕はサンダルを脱いで板の間に上がった。
lines.english: After swearing it upon Orion high overhead, I removed the sandals and stepped onto the wooden floor.

lines.japanese: このまま意欲まで冷めないうちに、さっさと机へ向かってしまおう。
lines.english: I should hurry to my desk before my resolve cooled with my body.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん……？」
lines.english: “Big brother...?”

lines.japanese: そのとき声がした。
lines.english: A voice spoke.

lines.japanese: 「さむいよう……」
lines.english: “It’s cooold…”

lines.japanese: 僕の手はガラス戸を半分ほど閉めかけていたけど、びっくりして思わず全身ごと固まってしまった。
lines.english: My hand had drawn the glass door halfway shut. Startled, I froze with my entire body.
“Ko…”
“…Kobato?”

lines.japanese: 振りかえると居間のすみ、たんすの陰で、暗くて色の判別もつかない毛布がもぞもぞと蠢いていた。
lines.english: In a corner of the living room, behind the dresser, a blanket too dark for its color to be seen wriggled and stirred.

lines.japanese: 「閉めてー、はやくー」
lines.english: “Close it. Hurry…”
“Oh. Right…”

lines.japanese: 僕は戸惑いながらも、三重の戸を急いでひとつずつ閉ざした。
lines.english: Still bewildered, I hurriedly closed each of the three doors in turn.

lines.japanese: 「さむいー、さむいー」
lines.english: “Cold, cold…”

lines.japanese: さまざまに形を変えるシルエットは、あたかも中で仔猫が遊んでいる布袋みたいだった。
lines.english: The silhouette shifted through a succession of shapes, like a cloth sack with a kitten playing inside.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は寝惚けているようだ。それはたしかに聞きなれた妹の声でありながら、初めて耳にする別人のそれのようでもあった。
lines.english: Kobato appeared to be half asleep. The voice was unmistakably my sister’s, familiar to me, yet it sounded like that of a stranger I had never heard before.

lines.japanese: 「なんでこんな時間に窓開けるのー、もぉー」
lines.english: “Why’re you opening the window this late? Honestly…”

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめん、いたの気付かなかったから……」
lines.english: “S-sorry. I didn’t realize you were there…”

lines.japanese: 僕は弱々しく弁解しながら、そろそろと部屋の中央まで進む。
lines.english: Offering my feeble excuse, I edged toward the center of the room.

lines.japanese: 「ひどーい」
lines.english: “That’s so mean.”

lines.japanese: 暗がりの中で影が盛りあがった。妹が上体を起こしたみたいだ。
lines.english: The shadow swelled in the darkness. My sister seemed to have sat up.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、すぐそうやっていじわるするー」
lines.english: “You’re always so mean to me, big brother.”

lines.japanese: 「意地悪って……」
lines.english: “Mean…?”

lines.japanese: 思わず繰りかえした。僕が相手のときはいつも言葉少なにぼそぼそ喋る小鳩の口から、耳慣れない声の耳慣れない台詞が飛びだした。
lines.english: I echoed the word without thinking. Kobato always mumbled as few words as possible to me; now an unfamiliar line in an unfamiliar voice had sprung from her mouth.

lines.japanese: いったい……どんな夢を見てたんだろう。
lines.english: What in the world… had she been dreaming?

lines.japanese: そもそも小鳩って、これまで僕を「お兄ちゃん」なんてアットホームな愛称で呼んだことがあったろうか？
lines.english: For that matter, had Kobato ever called me anything so homey as ‘big brother’ before?

lines.japanese: じゃあ、なんて呼ばれてたのかって記憶を辿れば、思いだされるのは「あの」とか「ねえ」とか、人称代名詞未満の他人行儀な呼びかけばかりだ。
lines.english: When I searched my memory for what she did call me, all I found were distant little summons—‘um’ and ‘hey’—that fell short even of personal pronouns.

lines.japanese: 「もう！　お兄ちゃん！」
lines.english: “Oh, big brother!”
“Y-yes…”

lines.japanese: 僕はちょっとくすぐったくなって、暗闇の真ん中に手を伸ばした。
lines.english: Something tickled inside me, and I reached into the center of the darkness.

lines.japanese: 「あの、電気付けるよ？」
lines.english: “Um, I’m going to turn on the light, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「ふえぇぇ、まぶしいぃぃ」
lines.english: “Nnngh, too briiight…”

lines.japanese: フライングでじたばたと畳を叩く音が聞こえた。
lines.english: Ahead of schedule, I heard her flailing hands strike the tatami.

lines.japanese: 「まだ付けてないってば……」
lines.english: “I haven’t turned it on yet…”

lines.japanese: なんだか、よその知らない子と話してる気分になってきた。
lines.english: I was beginning to feel as though I were speaking with somebody else’s child.

lines.japanese: はぁ……。
lines.english: Haaah…

lines.japanese: 僕は漏らす溜息に合わせて蛍光灯のスイッチを引いた。まばゆい白光が弾け、八畳ばかりの和室と寝惚けまなこの妹の体を照らしだす。
lines.english: In time with the sigh escaping me, I pulled the fluorescent light’s cord. Dazzling white light burst over the small room and my sister’s sleep-dazed form.

lines.japanese: すると──
lines.english: And then—
“What?”

lines.japanese: ──照らしだされた毛布の下は、目に鮮やかな素肌の一色だった。
lines.english: Beneath the blanket, now exposed to the light, was nothing but a vivid expanse of bare skin.

lines.japanese: 「ほらー、やっぱりまぶしぃー」
lines.english: “See? I told you it was briiight.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ごご、ごめんっ！」
lines.english: “Oh—s-s-sorry!”

lines.japanese: 視界に一瞬とびこんできた胸元が、なだらかな隆起を見せていた。
lines.english: For an instant, I had seen the gentle curve of her chest.

lines.japanese: いきなり妹の順調な発育を目の当たりにして、僕は気まずいとか照れくさいとか、もちろん嬉しいとか、そんなことを思う余裕さえなかった。
lines.english: Confronted without warning by the evidence that my sister was growing up, I had no room to feel awkward or embarrassed—much less pleased.

lines.japanese: 「い、いま消すから！」
lines.english: “I-I’ll turn it off!”

lines.japanese: カチカチカチカチぶちっ！
lines.english: Click-click-click-click—snap!

lines.japanese: 「うあっ！」
lines.english: “Ah!”

lines.japanese: 気が急くあまり蛍光灯の紐を四回も引いてしまった。
lines.english: In my panic, I had pulled the cord four times.

lines.japanese: しかも照明が振り出しに戻ったところで、それはお約束のようにちぎれてしまった。
lines.english: And just as the light returned to its starting state, the cord broke, with the inevitability of a well-worn comedy routine.
“Oh… oh…”

lines.japanese: 「なにー、どしたのー？」
lines.english: “Huh? What’s wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「ち、ちがっ……わざとじゃないよ！？」
lines.english: “I-it’s not—! I didn’t mean to, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「なにがー？」
lines.english: “Mean to do what?”

lines.japanese: うろたえる兄と対照的に、半裸の妹は呑気。まるで立場が逆だ。
lines.english: I was flustered; my half-naked little sister, by contrast, was perfectly unconcerned. It was as though our roles were reversed.

lines.japanese: 「こ、小鳩っ……はやく服、服をっ」
lines.english: “K-Kobato… Hurry and put on your clothes.”
“Clothes…?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は眩しそうにまぶたをきつく閉じながら、両手をぱたぱたさせて傍らに積まれていた衣類の山を探るように叩いた。
lines.english: Eyes squeezed shut against the light, Kobato patted blindly with both hands at the pile of clothing beside her.

lines.japanese: 「あれー、お兄ちゃんの服ないよー」
lines.english: “Huh? Big Brother, your clothes aren’t here.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、おれのじゃなくて……ああもう」
lines.english: “Not mine—yours. Oh, for…”

lines.japanese: 僕はあわてて小鳩の前に膝をつき、はだけていた毛布を引きよせて、彼女の顔以外をすっぽりくるんでやった。
lines.english: I hurriedly knelt before her, drew in the fallen edges of the blanket, and wrapped her completely, leaving only her face exposed.
“Haaah…”

lines.japanese: 一息ついて頭を垂れる。
lines.english: I let out a breath and hung my head.

lines.japanese: そうやって僕が思わず表情を隠したのは、兄として、こんなことぐらいで赤くなってるところなんか見られたくなかったからかもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps I hid my face because, as her brother, I did not want her to see me blush over something so trivial.

lines.japanese: でも、だって、僕は女の子の裸なんて、本やインターネットでしか見たことがなかったんだ。赤くなると言っても、決していやらしい気持ちじゃない。不可抗力っていうか免疫不全っていうか──
lines.english: But I had never seen a girl undressed outside books and the internet. And even if I blushed, it was not from any indecent feeling. It was an involuntary reaction, a lack of immunity—

lines.japanese: ──つまり、ちょっとぐらいドキッとするのは仕方ないことなんだ。
lines.english: —in other words, I couldn’t help it if my heart skipped a beat or two.
“…What?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の低いつぶやきが聞こえて、僕は下げていた頭をもたげた。
lines.english: At Kobato’s low murmur, I raised my bowed head.

lines.japanese: 彼女は光に慣れた目を大きく見開いて僕の顔をじっと見る。どうやら夢の世界から帰還したみたいだ。
lines.english: Her eyes, now accustomed to the light, opened wide and stared at my face. It appeared she had returned from the world of dreams.

lines.japanese: 「はは……おはよ。目、覚めた？」
lines.english: “Ha ha… Good morning. Awake now?”
“…Who are you?”

lines.japanese: 「誰って……」
lines.english: “Who…?”

lines.japanese: 前言撤回。小鳩はいまだ夢うつつの狭間みたいだ。
lines.english: I took it back. Kobato still hovered at the border between dream and waking.

lines.japanese: 「あのね？　この家にはいま、君と僕しかいないんだけど」
lines.english: “Listen. You and I are the only people in this house right now.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の眉がぴくりと跳ねる。風に揺れる草原みたいに表情がざわっと動き、目に見えて紅潮していった。
lines.english: Kobato’s eyebrows twitched. Emotion rustled across her face like wind through a field of grass, and color visibly flooded her cheeks.

lines.japanese: 「あはは……」
lines.english: “Ah-ha-ha…”

lines.japanese: なんだか無言で非難されてる気がして、僕は無意識のうちに硬い愛想笑いを浮かべていた。
lines.english: I felt accused by her silence and found an unconscious, rigid smile fixed upon my face.

lines.japanese: 僕の笑顔を置き去りにして、小鳩は真っ赤になった顔を深々と伏せた。裸身を覆う毛布をいっそう引きよせ、その中で縮こまるように身じろぎする。
lines.english: Leaving my smile unanswered, Kobato bowed her scarlet face. She pulled the blanket more tightly over herself and shrank within it.

lines.japanese: 「見られちゃった……」
lines.english: “You saw me…”

lines.japanese: 畳の上にぽつりと落とされた一言。
lines.english: The words dropped alone onto the tatami.

lines.japanese: 相手を責めることなく自己完結している言葉は、僕に対するいつもの羽田小鳩らしい反応だった。
lines.english: She blamed no one; the whole thing began and ended with her. It was exactly the sort of response I knew from Kobato Haneda.

lines.japanese: 「あ……いや、見てないよ？」
lines.english: “Oh… No. I didn’t see anything.”

lines.japanese: 僕は思わず嘘をついた。
lines.english: The lie escaped before I could stop it.

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん……分か、分かった……じゃあ、いいです……」
lines.english: “Oh. Okay… I—I understand… Then it’s fine…”

lines.japanese: 僕の気休めみたいな嘘を、むりやり信じることにしたみたいだ。毛布の合わせから先端だけ覗いている彼女の指が、胸の上あたりで毛羽立った表面をきゅっと握っていた。
lines.english: She seemed to force herself to believe the little lie I had offered for comfort. Only the tips of her fingers showed through the blanket’s overlapping edges, clutching its fleecy surface tight against her chest.

lines.japanese: 僕は愛敬を振りまくように兄貴らしいことを口にしてみる。
lines.english: Trying to charm my way through it, I said something suitably big-brotherly.

lines.japanese: 「なに、どうしたの、そんな格好で。風邪ひくよ」
lines.english: “What happened? Why were you dressed like that? You’ll catch cold.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はいちど黒目がちな瞳でゆっくり僕を見上げたが──
lines.english: Kobato slowly looked up at me with her dark, wide eyes—

lines.japanese: 「うん。気を付ける」
lines.english: “Okay. I’ll be careful.”

lines.japanese: ──すぐに目蓋を伏せた。
lines.english: —then immediately lowered them again.

lines.japanese: 余計な気遣いだったかもしれない。人間は恒温動物なんだ。真冬に毛布一枚で寝るものじゃないなんて、そんなことは言葉を覚えるより先に知ってる。
lines.english: Perhaps the concern had been needless. Human beings were warm-blooded animals. She had known since before she learned words that one did not sleep under a single blanket in midwinter.

lines.japanese: 「あの……ごめん、お風呂でのぼせちゃって、ちょっと横になってただけ……」
lines.english: “Um… Sorry. I got overheated in the bath, so I only lay down for a little while…”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が僕に毛布の背中を向けながら、ぼそぼそと付けくわえた。
lines.english: Turning her blanket-wrapped back to me, Kobato added in a mumble.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ。のぼせてって、実はおれもなんだけど、あはは、似たもの兄妹」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. The bath got me too, actually. Ha ha. Like brother, like sister.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm.”

lines.japanese: 生返事と共に剥きだしの細い腕が一本、合わせの奥からにょっきり現れ、脱ぎすててあった服の山を掻きよせる。
lines.english: With the absent reply, one slender bare arm emerged from the blanket and raked the discarded pile of clothes closer.

lines.japanese: 見慣れた部屋着のあいだから、見慣れない淡色の太い紐がはみ出て垂れさがっていた。
lines.english: Among the familiar clothes she wore around the house hung a thick, pale strap I did not recognize.

lines.japanese: ふと、目にしたばかりの膨らみかけを思いだす。僕の妹も、いつの間にか胸に下着を付ける歳になっていたらしい。
lines.english: The budding curve I’d just glimpsed came back to mind. Somewhere along the way, my sister had reached the age where she wore a bra.

lines.japanese: 見てはいけないものを見てしまった気がして、僕は思わず顔を背けた。しかし突然のことで、ちょっと不自然な動きだったかもしれない。
lines.english: Feeling I had seen something forbidden, I turned my face away. The movement was so sudden that it may have looked rather unnatural.

lines.japanese: 立ちあがってこの場を去るべきかとも思ったけど、いますぐそうするのはもっと不自然だろうか。
lines.english: I considered standing and leaving, but perhaps doing so immediately would seem even more unnatural.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ……」
lines.english: “Well, then…”

lines.japanese: 逃げるタイミングを逸してしまった兄より、妹の方が先に腰を上げた。視線の交換さえなかった。毛布の裳裾が畳をこすって遠ざかる。
lines.english: My sister got to her feet before I did; I’d missed my chance to make an escape. We didn’t even exchange a glance. The hem of the blanket whispered across the tatami as she moved away.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、小鳩」
lines.english: “Um, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: なんとなく小さな声で呼びとめると、彼女はびくりと肩を揺らすように立ちどまり──
lines.english: When I stopped her with the faint, almost idle summons, her shoulders jumped—

lines.japanese: ──首から上だけで小さく振りかえった。
lines.english: —and she looked slightly back, turning only her head.

lines.japanese: そして口を開くこともなく次の言葉を待っている。
lines.english: Without opening her mouth, she waited for me to continue.

lines.japanese: また余計な気遣いかもしれないけど、と思いながら僕は訊いた。
lines.english: Thinking again that it might be needless concern, I asked:

lines.japanese: 「もう平気なの？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling all right now?”

lines.japanese: 「え……な、なにが？」
lines.english: “What…? A-all right from what?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、湯当たり」
lines.english: “From getting overheated in the bath.”

lines.japanese: 「え、だって……風呂でのぼせたんだよね？」
lines.english: “I mean, you got overheated in the bath, right?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、膝をついたままの僕と立ちあがった小鳩とのあいだに、コントの「間」みたいな沈黙が流れた。
lines.english: For a moment, between me kneeling on the floor and Kobato standing before me, there passed a silence with the timing of a comedy sketch.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、うん、もう大丈夫」
lines.english: “Oh! Right. I’m fine now.”

lines.japanese: そして妹が思いだしたように口を開いた。
lines.english: My sister spoke as though she had just remembered.

lines.japanese: 「ほんとに？」
lines.english: “Are you sure?”

lines.japanese: まだ寝惚けてる気がするけど……。
lines.english: She still seemed half asleep…

lines.japanese: こっくり。しかし彼女は無言でうなずいた。
lines.english: A little nod. She answered without a word.

lines.japanese: 大丈夫かな……風邪ひいて熱っぽいとかじゃなければいいんだけど。
lines.english: Would she really be all right? I hoped she had not caught a cold and developed a fever.

lines.japanese: でも僕は、彼女が兄に心配されるのを好まない子だって知っている。
lines.english: But I knew she disliked being worried over by her brother.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……体冷えてると思うから、温かくしないと。今年の風邪はたち悪いらしいよ」
lines.english: “Um… You’re probably chilled, so make sure you warm up. I hear this year’s cold is particularly nasty.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ありがと。うん。気を付ける」
lines.english: “Th-thanks. I will. I’ll be careful.”

lines.japanese: なんだか、ふたりして模範的兄妹のマニュアルでも読んでるみたいな会話だった。
lines.english: The exchange sounded as though we were both reading from a handbook for exemplary siblings.

lines.japanese: やっぱりだ。思ったとおり、大した言葉はかけられなかった。
lines.english: Just as I had thought. I had failed to find anything meaningful to say.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ええと……」
lines.english: “Well, then… um…”

lines.japanese: 「……おやすみ」
lines.english: “…Good night.”

lines.japanese: 「おやすみなさい」
lines.english: “Good night.”

lines.japanese: 小さな体には大きすぎる毛布を、小鳩は魔法使いのローブみたいにずるずる引きずって二階へ消えていった。
lines.english: Dragging the blanket, far too large for her little body, like a wizard’s robe, Kobato disappeared upstairs.

lines.japanese: ひとり残された和室。紐が切れた蛍光灯は、白々しいぐらいに明るかった。
lines.english: I remained alone in the living room. The fluorescent light with its broken cord shone almost offensively bright.

lines.japanese: 僕は素足で畳を擦りながら思う。この家の兄妹はなんでこういつも、久しぶりに再会したいとこ同士みたいにぎくしゃくしてるんだろう。
lines.english: I rubbed one bare foot against the tatami and wondered why the siblings of this house were always so awkward together, like cousins meeting again after years apart.

lines.japanese: 静まりかえった羽田邸。
lines.english: The Haneda house lay utterly still.

lines.japanese: 兄のさだめを知らない妹。
lines.english: A little sister ignorant of her brother’s fate.

lines.japanese: このところ、しばしば思う。
lines.english: Lately, a thought often came to me.

lines.japanese: 僕がいなくなったあと、彼女は寂しい思いをしてくれるだろうか。
lines.english: After I was gone, would she feel lonely?

lines.japanese: もしさよならを告げたら、彼女は僕を引きとめてくれるだろうか。
lines.english: If I told her goodbye, would she ask me to stay?

lines.japanese: 僕は畳の居間を渡り、照明の壁スイッチを押して、まぶしすぎる白光にお引き取りを願った。
lines.english: I crossed the tatami room and pressed the switch on the wall, inviting that overbright white light to depart.

lines.japanese: ちぎれてしまった紐はあした明るいうちに結びなおしておこう。なんとなく、いまはそんな気分じゃない。
lines.english: I would tie the broken cord again tomorrow, while it was light. Somehow, I did not feel like doing it now.

lines.japanese: 部屋を出るとき、ふと“残務処理”のことを思いだした。
lines.english: As I left the room, my Unfinished Business returned to mind.

lines.japanese: 五番目の課題は“妹と仲良くなる”にでもしようかな。
lines.english: Perhaps the fifth item should be ‘Grow closer to my sister.’

lines.japanese: べつに、いまでも仲が悪いわけじゃないんだけどさ。
lines.english: It was not as though we were on bad terms now.
